THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County set new zoning rules for battery storage and data centers and punted a major wind energy resolution back to committee, while Wausau advanced funding for lead pipe replacement and a downtown development project.

  • Marathon County adopted a 500-foot setback rule for battery energy storage systems and a temporary moratorium on data centers, then referred the Hub City Wind project resolution back to the Executive Committee for a clearer recommendation at the September board meeting.
  • The Wausau Finance Committee approved a tax increment revenue bond for the Foundry on Third development and a 2026 budget workshop calendar, with four sessions beginning October 5 at 6:30 p.m.
  • Wausau's Board of Public Works approved roughly $1.2 million in pay estimates for lead service line replacement and Stark Street construction, and hired Clark Dietz for a sanitary sewer capacity study.
  • The Wausau Police & Fire Commission launched a deputy chief promotional process — applications open in September, with a decision expected at the December meeting — framed as early succession planning for the police chief role.
  • Weston's Parks Committee gave Everest Youth Hockey the green light to develop a feasibility plan for a 30,000-square-foot indoor community space at Kennedy Park, with no village funds committed.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board is set to vote on accepting the Village Clerk's resignation, following a special meeting called for August 27.

Coming up: Wausau's Committee of the Whole meets Wednesday, September 2 at 5:30 p.m. and could take up items advanced by the Finance Committee this week; also watch Tuesday's Economic Development Committee meeting at 5:30 p.m. for downtown project activity.
